newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stainless industry uses less nickel in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German stainless industry uses less nickel in 1996.

text.p: German stainless steel producers would use an estimated 72,000-75,000 tonnes of nickel in 1996, down from 90,000 tonnes last year, a spokeswoman at steel producers' association WVS said on Thursday.
This followed a decline in output and prices of stainless steel, she said in response to an enquiry.
But nickel use was set to recover in 1997 along with an expected increase in stainless steel production by three to five percent.
Stainless steel accounts for two thirds of nickel uses.

German output of stainless steel ingot, the raw material for the production of long and flat finished products, was estimated at 1.35 million tonnes in 1996, down from 1.49 million in 1995, as consumer industries ordered less.
Precise stainless steel consumption figures were not available but should be near output because exports and imports were well balanced, the spokeswoman said.

Members of the specialty steel trade association, Edelstahlhandels-Vereinigung (EHV), expected sharply lower revenue from their stockholding and processing activities than last year's two billion marks, she added.
This was due to rising trade stocks, falling demand and inventory devaluations.
But EHV noted stockholders' supplies were now at 65 and 70 days of use compared with 80-90 in mid-1996 in a recent reversal of the weak conditions earlier this year.
Stainless mills were reporting higher orders, which boded well for the anticipated recovery in 1997. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
